nodes.description: The recurrent heterozygous de novo c.2011C>T p.(Arg671Trp) variant changes a conserved residue in the C-terminal part of MTSS2, outside the membrane-binding I-BAR domain. MTSS2 binds ATP-actin monomers through its WH2 domain and deforms PI(4,5)P2-rich membranes through its I-BAR domain; the effect of the variant on these activities has not been measured, so they are bound without a modifier. Patient fibroblasts have normal MTSS2 protein levels.

evidence.snippet: Here we report five individuals with the same heterozygous de novo variant in MTSS2 (GenBank: NM_138383.2: c.2011C>T ... ) identified by exome sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: ABBA regulates plasma-membrane and actin dynamics to promote radial glia extension.
evidence.snippet: ABBA binds ATP-actin monomers with high affinity and deforms PtdIns(4,5)P(2)-rich membranes in vitro through its WH2 and IM domains, respectively.

genetic_context.description: NM_138383.2:c.2011C>T, p.(Arg671Trp), heterozygous in every reported patient and de novo in each one whose parents were tested. In a fly rescue assay it behaves as a partial loss of function, and it is toxic when overexpressed in flies; in mouse cortex it does not act as a dominant negative on RhoA activation or progenitor division. No functional_impact_category is set because these readings disagree.

nodes.description: In embryonic mouse cortex, expression of MTSS2 R671W disorganized radial glial fibres, kept progenitors in the ventricular and subventricular zones, and left neurons multipolar with few bipolar migrating cells, without changing the number of dividing cells. The authors suggest the variant acts mainly after cell division, for example on migration. MTSS2 (ABBA) normally regulates actin and membrane dynamics in radial glia, and depleting it impairs radial glial process extension.

nodes.description: At the cleavage furrow of dividing radial glial progenitors, Mtss2 recruits the scaffold protein Nedd9 and promotes RhoA activity. Knocking Mtss2 down in embryonic mouse cortex blocks cytokinesis, followed by apoptosis, and halts progenitor proliferation. This branch rests on knockdown: the patient variant expressed with wild-type Mtss2 neither reduced RhoA activation nor changed the number of dividing cells, so it is marked provisional. The module node is framed around the centrosome and spindle, whereas Mtss2 acts at the cleavage furrow.

nodes.description: In flies, loss of the ortholog mim reduces synaptic transmission. In mice, Mtss1l (MTSS2) is induced in activated dentate granule cells and is needed for activity-dependent increases in dendritic spines and excitatory currents, and ABBA is enriched in parvalbumin-positive interneurons and drives spine initiation in cultured neurons. Whether synaptic function is impaired in patients has not been studied.
